proposals.premise: Three timed sound stops make route choice the primary task; photographs and available audio support decisions without replacing timing and access information.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows the route beside three ordered stop cards; phone starts with the next stop, timing, and route choice, with one photograph sharing the screen.
proposals.move: Choose the direct or step-free route; the ordered stops update immediately, showing the next reachable stop and whether the choir remains available before 20:30.
proposals.tradeoff: The sequence is quick to understand and operate one-handed, but photographs and previews remain secondary to practical route information.

proposals.premise: Visitors may assume every sound location is a stopping point, but the narrow bridge path requires an organization around movement and reachability.
proposals.opening: Desktop opens with a route strip and large current-stage panel; phone opens with “keep moving” at the bridge, while timing and the bridge photograph share space.
proposals.move: Tap “route me onward”; the next reachable stop appears in the same panel, using the step-free alternate route to the far side when selected.
proposals.tradeoff: This prevents the bridge from reading as a group stop and makes access explicit, but the three sounds feel less like equal attractions.
